power.title: Power Analysis Check
report:
::: {.callout-tip title="Learn More" collapse="true"}

Power analyses need to contain the following information to be interpretable: the type of power analysis, the statistical test, the software used, sample size, critical alpha criterion, power level, effect size, and an effect size metric. In addition, it is recommended to make sure the power analysis is reproducible (by sharing the code, or a screenshot, of the power analysis), and to provide good arguments for why the study was designed to detect an effect of this size.

For an a-priori power analysis, where the sample size is determined, reporting all information would look like:

> An a priori power analysis for an independent samples t-test, conducted using the pwr.t.test function from pwr (Champely, 2020), indicated that for a Cohen's d = 0.5, an alpha level of 0.05, and a desired power level of 80% required at least 64 participants in each group.

For a sensitivity power analysis, this sentence would look like:

> A sensitivity power analysis for an independent samples t-test, conducted using the pwr.t.test function from pwr (Champely, 2020), indicated that with 64 participants in each group, and an alpha level of 0.05, a desired power level of 80% was reached for an effect size of d = 0.5.

:::

text.text: Background: With the rapid advancement of artificial intelligence (AI), large language models (LLMs) such as ChatGPT have demonstrated strong potential to transform healthcare research and practice.
However, LLMs are probabilistic and generate inherently variable outputs, which create risk and uncertainty in healthcare applications.

Therefore, analyzing the current research landscape of ChatGPT applications is imperative to understand applied techniques and related concerns and to facilitate their practical integration into healthcare information systems.

Objective: Leveraging LLM-based agentic AI with domain experts to analyze trends in ChatGPT healthcare applications and to examine the collaborative and interpretative capacities of LLM agents in broader contexts beyond narrowly defined topics.

Methods: The review used a systematic search of the PubMed and Web of Science databases, following PRISMA-ScR guidelines, and focused on ChatGPT applications, associated concerns, applied techniques, and usage factors.

To support the review process, an adaptive, iterative LLMbased agentic AI with a human-in-the-loop mechanism was employed for automated metadata extraction, identification, classification, and knowledge synthesis.

text.text: Driven by practical demands, the evolution of related LLM technology has progressed from preliminary zero-shot prompting to more structured few-shot paradigms that incorporate explicit task instructions and self-verification mechanisms to achieve more accurate responses.

text.text: Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) enables LLMs to access up-to-date external knowledge, improving factual accuracy and reducing hallucinations.
Results from using LLMs with RAG technology show that LLMs can be effective at a lower cost and can efficiently prevent hallucinations [16].

text.text: Building on foundation LLMs, agentic AI further integrates LLM agents, prompt engineering, RAG technologies, and reasoning enhancements into a workflow that supports multi-agent collaboration and coordinated autonomy.
As a result, agentic AI can exhibit goal-directed behavior, dynamic adaptation, and self-improvement [22].
text.formatted: As a result, agentic AI can exhibit goal-directed behavior, dynamic adaptation, and self-improvement <ref type="bibr" target="#b22">[22]</ref>.

text.formatted: Consequently, it has been increasingly deployed in research automation and medical decision support <ref type="bibr" target="#b17">[17]</ref>.

text.text: Gridach et al. [18] investigated agentic AI for scientific discovery to address system reliability and automate literature reviews, emphasizing the importance of human-AI collaboration.
text.formatted: Gridach et al. <ref type="bibr" target="#b18">[18]</ref> investigated agentic AI for scientific discovery to address system reliability and automate literature reviews, emphasizing the importance of human-AI collaboration.

text.text: In addition, agentic AI demonstrates adaptability, advanced decision-making, and self-sufficiency, enabling it to operate dynamically in evolving environments to pursue complex goals with minimal human intervention [19].
text.formatted: In addition, agentic AI demonstrates adaptability, advanced decision-making, and self-sufficiency, enabling it to operate dynamically in evolving environments to pursue complex goals with minimal human intervention <ref type="bibr" target="#b19">[19]</ref>.

text.text: However, one major limitation of LLMs is their tendency to hallucinate false or irrelevant information [23].
text.formatted: However, one major limitation of LLMs is their tendency to hallucinate false or irrelevant information <ref type="bibr" target="#b23">[23]</ref>.

text.text: As a result, it is difficult for users to determine whether the provided answers are grounded in appropriate facts [24].
text.formatted: As a result, it is difficult for users to determine whether the provided answers are grounded in appropriate facts <ref type="bibr" target="#b24">[24]</ref>.

text.text: Additionally, scholars suggested that several barriers hinder clinical use, including the lack of up-to-date medical information, failure to consider specific patient circumstances, and insufficient medical expertise and background to understand the complex relationships between conditions and treatments [7, 8].
text.formatted: Additionally, scholars suggested that several barriers hinder clinical use, including the lack of up-to-date medical information, failure to consider specific patient circumstances, and insufficient medical expertise and background to understand the complex relationships between conditions and treatments <ref type="bibr" target="#b6">[7,</ref> <ref type="bibr" target="#b7">8]</ref>.

text.text: Moreover, medical AI tools can become unreliable due to biases in the training data, both known and unknown, which may reflect societal inequities [25].
text.formatted: Moreover, medical AI tools can become unreliable due to biases in the training data, both known and unknown, which may reflect societal inequities <ref type="bibr" target="#b25">[25]</ref>.

text.text: Furthermore, healthcare organizations that aim to implement ChatGPT would need comprehensive guidelines for handling patient data and implementing measures to secure patient privacy [15].
text.formatted: Furthermore, healthcare organizations that aim to implement ChatGPT would need comprehensive guidelines for handling patient data and implementing measures to secure patient privacy <ref type="bibr" target="#b15">[15]</ref>.

text.text: Additionally, AI models are often unable to trace the evidence line, making auditability and verification difficult [26].
text.formatted: Additionally, AI models are often unable to trace the evidence line, making auditability and verification difficult <ref type="bibr" target="#b26">[26]</ref>.

text.text: Unlike traditional rule-based, deterministic information technologies, LLMs are probabilistic, data-driven, and inherently intangible (black-box) [27], thereby generating capricious, unpredictable outputs.
text.formatted: Unlike traditional rule-based, deterministic information technologies, LLMs are probabilistic, data-driven, and inherently intangible (black-box) <ref type="bibr" target="#b27">[27]</ref>, thereby generating capricious, unpredictable outputs.

text.text: As a result, scholars noted that whether AI-based technologies actually deliver improved outcomes and added value to healthcare remains unanswered [28].
text.formatted: As a result, scholars noted that whether AI-based technologies actually deliver improved outcomes and added value to healthcare remains unanswered <ref type="bibr" target="#b28">[28]</ref>.

text.text: However, despite these challenges, applying LLMs has significant potential to enhance multiple aspects of healthcare [29].
text.formatted: However, despite these challenges, applying LLMs has significant potential to enhance multiple aspects of healthcare <ref type="bibr" target="#b29">[29]</ref>.

text.text: The coexistence of opportunities and challenges can lead to either stagnation or progress, warranting further investigation.

Given the numerous barriers and challenges, analyzing the current research landscape and summarizing major application trends are imperative for developing a comprehensive understanding of these technologies, facilitating practical applications, and guiding future research.
Such reviews help identify knowledge gaps, enabling more systematic advancement of research [30].
text.formatted: Such reviews help identify knowledge gaps, enabling more systematic advancement of research <ref type="bibr" target="#b30">[30]</ref>.

text.text: Lai et al. noted that the rapid pace of medical progress and evidence turnover has increased the demand for timely evidence synthesis, and that literature reviews can integrate and evaluate existing research to guide clinical decisions [31].
text.formatted: Lai et al. noted that the rapid pace of medical progress and evidence turnover has increased the demand for timely evidence synthesis, and that literature reviews can integrate and evaluate existing research to guide clinical decisions <ref type="bibr" target="#b31">[31]</ref>.

text.text: However, literature review processes are predominantly manual and time-intensive, requiring substantial effort for article screening, eligibility assessment, and data extraction, which becomes more difficult when researchers examine multiple themes, such as applications, techniques, and concerns, simultaneously.
In contrast, LLMs can process large volumes of literature simultaneously while providing rapid, iterative feedback to researchers.
This capability enables iterative refinement of the review, improving the efficiency and responsiveness of evidence synthesis within the review process.

This study integrates a review process with human-agentic AI collaboration, incorporating prompt engineering, RAG technology, and LLM agents to extract and identify metadata from medical journal articles.
The metadata extracted from the studies included: authors, title, publication date, journal, abstract, purpose, keywords, citation, applications, concerns, and usage factors.
The evidence-driven extracted data were used to cluster and classify ChatGPT applications, applied techniques, and associated concerns.
Through multiple data analyses, including temporal, thematic, and main path analyses [32, 33, 34], we trace knowledge flows and reveal critical trends in healthcare ChatGPT applications.

text.text: Initially, this study used 35 papers (see Supplementary file) from 16 medical journals as a groundtruth dataset to construct, evaluate, and iteratively refine prompting strategies, RAG retrievers, workflow component performance, and agent interaction, thereby optimizing agentic AI metadata extraction and identification results and reproducibility for subsequent multiple data analyses by domain experts.
The keywords "ChatGPT," "Healthcare," "Medical," "GenAI," and "Agentic AI" were used to search the Web of Science (WoS) Core Collection and EndNote PubMed database.
The search strategy was refined by publication year (2023-2025), open access status, and document type (article or review article).
In this study, 2 reviewers conducted the screening.
Only full-text articles were included in this scoping review to examine metadata related to ChatGPT applications, applied techniques, associated concerns, and usage factors.
An agentic AI workflow was used to handle data extraction and validation automatically.
Therefore, no further explicit inclusion or exclusion criteria were applied in this study.

Some LLM agents were employed to extract, identify, reason, and synthesize data from the included papers, while other agents assessed generated responses using an LLM-as-a-judge approach for grading and verification.
Within this iterative loop, human-AI cooperation was applied to optimize agent-generated responses.
Different metadata extraction and synthesis forms were stored in separate CSV file formats.
Finally, 3 reviewers validated the overall files and results.

A goal-convergent spiral approach was implemented in this study, beginning with a small dataset and progressing from coarse structural schema to progressively expanded datasets and more detailed tasks toward the intended objective.

Meanwhile, domain experts were integrated into the iterative human-AI collaborative agentic AI workflow to ensure accuracy and reproducibility. leverage external data sources, retrieve relevant information, and validate generative responses.

Throughout this pipeline, the human-in-the-loop approach ensures that data-driven discoveries are grounded in domain knowledge, validated appropriately, and translated into meaningful scientific advances rather than remaining isolated algorithmic outputs [35].

text.text: Nevertheless, even when prompts were not grammatically correct, LLM agents captured semantic intent and provided appropriate responses, reflecting a form of human-like communication observed in the agentic AI workflow.
However, when communication breaks down, as it often does, LLM agents may display rigidity and make assertions without following through.
From a probabilistic perspective, LLMs generate responses by sampling from high-probability regions of a conditional knowledge distribution.
While the outputs tend to appear, in effect, like "average/mean" answers, which LLMs proffered.
Prompt engineering and RAG constrain the probability distribution by introducing task-specific context with external knowledge, guiding the model toward more precise, context-aware outputs.

These observations suggest that prompt engineering, RAG technologies, and databases, along with agent interaction management such as answer checking and confirming, play an essential role throughout the development process.
Furthermore, prompt intention analysis, used to reconfirm user intent, can clarify the intended purpose during collaboration within an Agentic AI workflow.

text.text: This study examines LLM agents' abilities in content recognition and semantic understanding across multiple documents, as well as their communication behaviors, to help researchers and healthcare providers gain deeper insights into their interactive behavior.

Compared with traditional machine learning clustering and NLP topic modeling methods, LLMs offer more intuitive and interpretable grouping and classification, particularly when combined with prompt engineering and multi-agent refinement strategies.
These strategies are valuable because natural language is inherently ambiguous and difficult to define.

Given their human-like communication patterns, the LLM agent may serve as an interaction layer alternative to traditional Human-Machine Interface (HMI) or User Interface (UI) for decision support systems.
Additionally, AI-generated content may be used as a bridge between data-centric AI and knowledge-centric AI, through content generation, knowledge integration, and human-AI co-creation [47].

text.text: In this context, an adaptive, iterative refinement process of an agentic AI workflow that aligns with human oversight may contribute to more efficient, robust, and interpretable AI-enabled medical informatics studies.
Furthermore, studies show that applications are not confined to single-function use cases or domains but are increasingly expanding in scope and depth across diverse practices.
At the same time, these applications are accompanied by a growing set of associated concerns, usage factors, and rapidly evolving applied techniques.

Taken together, this indicates that focusing on any single dimension (such as ethics, safety, privacy, reliability, explainability, autonomy, or specific applied techniques) in isolation is insufficient.

Additionally, this calls for an overarching governance approach that systematically addresses the integration of applied technological advancements, the rapid expansion of applications, and the associated concerns from a management AI perspective to manage AI challenges, risks, and technology effectively.
Over time, concerns about the data and knowledge limitations of LLMs have declined, suggesting these issues have become well recognized rather than focal points of ongoing analysis.

In contrast, concerns related to human-AI collaboration and trust demonstrate a gradual increase, reflecting a shift in research emphasis from model-level limitations to interaction-and system-level challenges as LLMs are progressively integrated into real-world applications.

The substantial overlap between the specific concern types and the top factors influencing usage indicates that issues, such as hallucination, trust, interpretability, transparency, bias, uncertainty, and ethics, simultaneously act as both drivers and constraints of LLM adoption.
From 2025 onward, factors not ranked among the top 10 began to appear, including autonomy, emergent behavior, and ambiguity.
These developments align with the need for RAG and prompt engineering, alongside a growing focus on "Agent and Multi-agent" and "Agentic AI" techniques.

Overall, the study suggests that ChatGPT application development is moving from emergence to a growth phase, characterized by the mutually reinforcing evolution of applied techniques, application domains, and factors influencing usage, while the maturity phase remains in its early stages.
For individual use, LLM agents can serve as an auxiliary tool, helping with tasks such as text mining, knowledge understanding, and documentation, thereby saving time and increasing efficiency.
However, as advances in AI technology enhance the generative capabilities of LLM agents and make errors harder to detect, users may become increasingly dependent on the answers they provide.
Furthermore, in human-AI interaction, LLMs have been observed to tend to agree with users' viewpoints, potentially reinforcing users' existing beliefs and increasing the risk of overreliance.

Although the study found that overreliance was reported in only 4 of 192 papers across 368 factors influencing usage, scholars have recently paid attention to the risks of overreliance and to preventing overdependence [51, 52].

text.text: Such overreliance may cause problems and could diminish critical thinking, leading users to lose their style and rely solely on LLMs.
To mitigate unconscious overreliance, human or AI agents should know how to verify LLM answers that align with the user's intended meaning and requirements.

text.text: This study encountered several limitations during data extraction, identification, and synthesis.
First, variable publication date labels and locations across articles were difficult to identify.
As a result, in some cases, accepted dates were used instead of publication dates, suggesting that rulebased prompting may be needed.
Second, existing PDF parsers still struggle to accurately interpret graphics and certain tables.

However, these constraints do not undermine the study's examination of agentic AI's ability to identify, classify, and synthesize extracted data, nor the analysis of ChatGPT application trends by experts.

From a medical informatics perspective, LLMs demonstrate strong potential as text-mining tools for extracting information from unstructured academic literature; however, their probabilistic nature introduces non-deterministic synonyms.
In addition, heterogeneous terminology and reference formats across the papers further complicate consistent data identification and integration.
In this study, LLMs were used as normalization layers to harmonize citation structure and standardize terminology, thereby improving consistency in downstream analyses.

To enhance reproducibility and semantic stability, future research should incorporate standard libraries (such as UMLS and ICD-9/10) and rule-based procedures that follow the LLM normalization layer to standardize terminology.
Such hybrid approaches may support more deterministic vocabulary alignment, particularly for domain-specific factors that are not explicitly predefined.

While this study implemented a human-agentic AI collaboration workflow for metadata extraction, contextual synthesis, citation network construction, and database integration through iterative refinement, we focused primarily on output quality and result reproducibility for trend analysis.
Formal evaluation of the agentic system was not conducted, which is a key limitation of the present work.
The system-level performance and scalability of the agentic AI workflow were beyond the scope of this study and warrant further investigation.
The rapid expansion of LLMs and ChatGPT applications, along with the exponential growth of their user base, has far outpaced traditional IT systems.
Moreover, unlike traditional IT systems, which yield consistent outputs, LLMs generate variable responses and produce hallucinations.
These fundamental distinctions suggest that research on LLM adoption and sustained use may diverge significantly from conventional IT adoption frameworks.
It is worthwhile to explore the factors driving their adoption and continued use to inform future practical implementation.

text.text: Beyond being mere tools, LLM-based agents can dynamically adapt by adding tools as tasks require.
We therefore suggest that agentic AI can be viewed as a decision-making assistant rather than merely a tool.
We propose an approach that integrates an agentic AI workflow through literature review processes.
The integration enables a broader range of NLP tasks, including extracting information from sparse data, reasoning and understanding, classification and clustering, and summarizing article content.
Based on this method, the study provides a comprehensive overview of trends in ChatGPT applications, associated concerns, applied techniques, and usage factors in healthcare.
The findings further provide meaningful insights into the operational mechanisms of agentic AI, demonstrating the potential of human-AI collaboration for medical informatics research.
